solutions.fullSolution: V(s) is the old estimate; r+gamma*V(s') is a fresh one-sample re-estimate from what just happened. If r+gamma*V(s') > V(s) (better than expected), TD error is positive, so V(s) increases toward it. If r+gamma*V(s') < V(s) (worse than expected), TD error is negative and V(s) decreases. The update always nudges the old estimate toward what was actually observed.

Correctly forms the alpha-weighted update using the TD error.

solutions.fullSolution: Replace the exact expectation sum_s' P(s'|s,a)*max_a' Q*(s',a') with the single observed s': r + gamma*max_a' Q(s',a'). Since this one-sample estimate is noisy, take a small step alpha toward it rather than overwriting: Q_new(s,a) = Q_old(s,a) + alpha*[r + gamma*max_a' Q_old(s',a') - Q_old(s,a)].

criteria.description: Correctly distinguishes TD-learning's V^pi target from Q-learning's Q* target.
Correctly explains why the max_a' target makes Q-learning off-policy/exploration-tolerant.

solutions.fullSolution: TD-learning's target r+gamma*V(s') uses the actual next action taken under pi: it estimates V^pi, the value of the specific data-generating policy. Q-learning's target uses max_a' Q(s',a'), the best possible next action regardless of what was actually taken: it estimates Q*, optimal-behavior value, no matter which policy generated the data. This is why Q-learning tolerates (needs) an exploratory epsilon-greedy behavior policy: the target doesn't depend on the behavior policy's own suboptimality, an off-policy property.
